about: The access that Meternaut needs outside its own resource group. Meternaut holds no write right: every grant below only reads, and a change to Azure is made with the token of the person who approved it, so that Azure checks that person's own rights (docs/proposals/03-access-and-onboarding.md). The deployment workflow's identity holds no right there and must not get one (AGENTS.md rule 18), so a person who may assign roles at each place grants it. Each line of grants is one role of one identity at one place. An identity is what a function app runs as, and the principals that hold its grants are listed as its holders: the app's own system-assigned identity, found on the app with the option that siteOption names. While an app is moved between kinds of identity, both kinds are holders (a user-assigned one has a name), so that the app is never without access. The list retired records what an earlier version granted and must now be removed: either a custom role that is no longer wanted at all (every assignment of it, then the role), or, with replacedBy, a grant of an identity that an app no longer runs as (only that identity's own assignment: the role stays, because the grant that replaces it needs it). tools/access-requirements.py reads this file: it checks what is granted, grants what is missing only with --apply, and with retire removes what is retired, again only with --apply. On 2026-11-07 the owner ordered the undo of what Meternaut added to his API Management instance: the cases app reads no key any more, so the custom role that read one (W7) and its grant are retired, and retire removes every assignment of that role at the instance's resource group and below it, then the role. The deployment identity's own custom role in that group (W8) is retired the same way, because no Hub action uses it since the actions that made objects on the instance were removed. R4 and R5, the usage app's reads of the gateway's telemetry, stay for now. docs/proposals/03-access-and-onboarding.md shows the two tables that the tool prints, and a test keeps them the same.

places.estate: Each subscription that the Watch reads (the app setting SCOPE_SUBSCRIPTIONS), or a management group above them
places.gatewayGroup: The resource group of the owner's API Management instance, and everything below it
places.centralWorkspace: The central workspace that the component writes to
places.projectGroup: The project's own resource group, where Meternaut plants waste of its own

Meternaut usage reader.description: Reads one table (AppMetrics, the metrics of workspace-based Application Insights) of the central workspace, so that the usage copy job of Meternaut can read the gateway token metrics. Nothing else.

grants.why: Reads the resources, their tags and management locks, Azure Advisor's cost recommendations, the platform metrics that Azure Monitor keeps for a resource and the pricing settings of the Microsoft Defender for Cloud plans: the detectors, the guards and the read-only tools of the investigator. It also reads a managed disk or a public IP address of the project's own resource group when the timer checks that a deleted resource is gone. The role reads and changes nothing
Reads the cost lines of every resource for the last 30 days, so that every figure is Cost Management's and never a model's
Reads the gateway's Application Insights component, where the gateway records the token metrics of every call
Reads one table (AppMetrics) of the central workspace. The component is workspace-based and the workspace asks for workspace permissions, so the role on the component alone returns no rows

retired.why: The writer of an earlier version: a custom role that read and deleted a managed disk and a public IP address in this group, held by this identity. Meternaut holds no write right now: a change is made with the token of the person who approved it, and Azure checks that person's own rights. The role's assignments and the role are removed with retire; the identity is removed by the deployment workflow or by the owner
Held by the user-assigned identity that the cases app ran as before its own system-assigned identity took over (R1). Only that identity's assignment is removed, and the role stays: R1 needs it
Held by the user-assigned identity that the cases app ran as before its own system-assigned identity took over (R2). Only that identity's assignment is removed, and the role stays: R2 needs it
Held by the user-assigned identity that the usage app ran as before its own system-assigned identity took over (R4). Only that identity's assignment is removed, and the role stays: R4 needs it
Held by the user-assigned identity that the usage app ran as before its own system-assigned identity took over (R5). Only that identity's assignment is removed, and the custom role stays: R5 needs it

A custom role of an earlier version that read one key of one subscription of the owner's API Management instance (and nothing else), so that the cases app could call the models through that instance. It was held by the cases app's own system-assigned identity and, before that, by this user-assigned identity. The owner ordered the undo of what Meternaut added to that instance on 2026-11-07, and the app reads no key any more: it calls the models of its own Foundry project with its own identity. Every assignment of the role at the instance's resource group and below it is removed, whoever holds it, and then the role itself

A custom role of the first environment that the deployment workflow's identity held in the resource group of the owner's API Management instance, so that the Hub could add Citadel's objects to the instance, attach an identity to it and make the access product of the first cases on it. No Hub action uses it since 2026-11-07: the owner ordered the undo of what Meternaut added to that instance, and the actions that made those objects were removed. Every assignment of the role at the instance's resource group and below it is removed, whoever holds it, and then the role itself. The identity stays: it deploys the project's own resource group, and it lives in the bootstrap group, so it is not looked up
